Implement the following plan:

# Organization Management & Member Invitations

## Context

Implement organization management UI to allow users to manage team members and send invitations using the Better Auth organizations plugin. The backend is already configured with roles (owner, admin, member) and permissions. This adds the frontend UI layer.

---

## File Structure

```
apps/web/src/
├── app/(app)/
│   ├── settings/
│   │   └── organization/
│   │       └── page.tsx                    # Organization settings page
│   └── invitations/
│       └── [invitationId]/
│           └── page.tsx                    # Invitation accept/reject page
│
└── components/organization/
    ├── index.ts
    ├── types.ts
    ├── member-list.tsx                     # Member table with actions
    ├── member-actions-menu.tsx             # Role change, remove member
    ├── invitation-list.tsx                 # Pending invitations
    ├── invite-member-dialog.tsx            # Responsive dialog/sheet
    ├── role-badge.tsx                      # Badge for owner/admin/member
    └── hooks/
        ├── index.ts
        ├── use-organization-members.ts
        ├── use-invitations.ts
        └── use-member-actions.ts
```

---

## Implementation Steps

### Step 1: Types & Hooks

**`components/organization/types.ts`**
```typescript
export type MemberRole = "owner" | "admin" | "member";
export type InvitationStatus = "pending" | "accepted" | "rejected" | "canceled";

export interface Member {
  id: string;
  userId: string;
  user: { id: string; name: string; email: string; image?: string };
  role: MemberRole;
  createdAt: Date;
}

export interface Invitation {
  id: string;
  email: string;
  role: MemberRole;
  status: InvitationStatus;
  expiresAt: Date;
  createdAt: Date;
}
```

**`components/organization/hooks/use-organization-members.ts`**
- Query for `authClient.organization.listMembers()`
- Returns `{ members, isLoading, refetch }`

**`components/organization/hooks/use-member-actions.ts`**
- Mutations for `removeMember`, `updateMemberRole`
- Invalidates queries on success, shows toast notifications

**`components/organization/hooks/use-invitations.ts`**
- Query for `authClient.organization.listInvitations()`
- Mutations for `inviteMember`, `cancelInvitation`

### Step 2: Role Badge Component

**`components/organization/role-badge.tsx`**
- Owner: primary variant
- Admin: secondary variant
- Member: outline variant

### Step 3: Member List Component

**`components/organization/member-list.tsx`**
- Table layout with columns: Avatar, Name, Email, Role, Joined, Actions
- Responsive: Table on desktop, Card list on mobile
- Member actions dropdown for admins/owners

**`components/organization/member-actions-menu.tsx`**
- Change Role submenu (member <-> admin, owner only for admin assignment)
- Remove member (confirmation dialog)
- Disabled for self and last owner

### Step 4: Invitation List Component

**`components/organization/invitation-list.tsx`**
- Shows pending invitations with email, role, expires date
- Cancel button for pending invitations
- Empty state when no invitations

### Step 5: Invite Member Dialog

**`components/organization/invite-member-dialog.tsx`**
- Responsive: Dialog on desktop, Sheet on mobile (use `useIsMobile`)
- Form with email input and role select
- Uses `@tanstack/react-form` + Zod (follow `create-organization-form.tsx` pattern)
- Success/error toasts with `sonner`

### Step 6: Settings Page

**`app/(app)/settings/organization/page.tsx`**
- Tabs: Members | Invitations
- Members tab: MemberList + InviteMemberDialog
- Invitations tab: InvitationList
- Page header with organization name

### Step 7: Invitation Acceptance Page

**`app/(app)/invitations/[invitationId]/page.tsx`**
- Fetch invitation via `authClient.organization.getInvitation()`
- Show organization name, role, inviter info
- Accept/Reject buttons
- Handle: not authenticated (redirect to sign in), expired, already accepted
- On accept: call `acceptInvitation`, set active org, redirect to dashboard

### Step 8: Navigation Updates

- Add "Settings" link to user menu (`components/user-menu.tsx`)
- Add to app sidebar if applicable

---

## Key Patterns to Follow

### Form Pattern (from create-organization-form.tsx)
```typescript
const form = useForm({
  defaultValues: { email: "", role: "member" },
  onSubmit: async ({ value }) => {
    const result = await authClient.organization.inviteMember({
      email: value.email,
      role: value.role,
    });
    if (result.error) {
      toast.error(result.error.message);
      return;
    }
    toast.success("Invitation sent");
    onSuccess?.();
  },
  validators: {
    onSubmit: z.object({
      email: z.string().email(),
      role: z.enum(["member", "admin"]),
    }),
  },
});
```

### Responsive Dialog/Sheet Pattern
```typescript
function InviteMemberDialog() {
  const isMobile = useIsMobile();
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);

  if (isMobile) {
    return (
      <Sheet open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen}>
        <SheetTrigger asChild><Button>Invite</Button></SheetTrigger>
        <SheetContent><InviteForm onSuccess={() => setOpen(false)} /></SheetContent>
      </Sheet>
    );
  }

  return (
    <Dialog open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen}>
      <DialogTrigger asChild><Button>Invite</Button></DialogTrigger>
      <DialogContent><InviteForm onSuccess={() => setOpen(false)} /></DialogContent>
    </Dialog>
  );
}
```

---

## API Methods (No new routes needed)

All operations use existing Better Auth client methods:

| Operation | Method |
|-----------|--------|
| List members | `authClient.organization.listMembers()` |
| Invite member | `authClient.organization.inviteMember({ email, role })` |
| Remove member | `authClient.organization.removeMember({ memberIdOrEmail })` |
| Update role | `authClient.organization.updateMemberRole({ memberId, role })` |
| List invitations | `authClient.organization.listInvitations()` |
| Cancel invitation | `authClient.organization.cancelInvitation({ invitationId })` |
| Get invitation | `authClient.organization.getInvitation({ id })` |
| Accept invitation | `authClient.organization.acceptInvitation({ invitationId })` |
| Reject invitation | `authClient.organization.rejectInvitation({ invitationId })` |

---

## Permission Rules

From `packages/auth/src/permissions.ts`:

- **Owner**: Full access, can assign admin role, manage billing
- **Admin**: Can invite/remove members, create/cancel invitations
- **Member**: Can view organization, cannot manage members

UI should hide action buttons for users without permission.

---

## Verification

1. Create organization, invite member via email
2. Accept invitation as new user
3. Verify member appears in list with correct role
4. Test role change (admin can change member role)
5. Test remove member (admin can remove members)
6. Test cancel invitation
7. Test responsive layouts (mobile/desktop)
8. Verify permission restrictions (member cannot see invite/manage buttons)

If this plan can be broken down into multiple independent tasks, consider using the TeamCreate tool to create a team and parallelize the work.

# Organization Management & Member Invitations

## Context

Implement organization management UI to allow users to manage team members and send invitations using the Better Auth organizations plugin. The backend is already configured with roles (owner, admin, member) and permissions. This adds the frontend UI layer.

---

## File Structure

```
apps/web/src/
├── app/(app)/
│   ├── settings/
│   │   └── organization/
│   │       └── page.tsx                    # Organization settings page
│   └── invitations/
│       └── [invitationId]/
│           └── page.tsx                    # Invitation accept/reject page
│
└── components/organization/
    ├── index.ts
    ├── types.ts
    ├── member-list.tsx                     # Member table with actions
    ├── member-actions-menu.tsx             # Role change, remove member
    ├── invitation-list.tsx                 # Pending invitations
    ├── invite-member-dialog.tsx            # Responsive dialog/sheet
    ├── role-badge.tsx                      # Badge for owner/admin/member
    └── hooks/
        ├── index.ts
        ├── use-organization-members.ts
        ├── use-invitations.ts
        └── use-member-actions.ts
```

---

## Implementation Steps

### Step 1: Types & Hooks

**`components/organization/types.ts`**
```typescript
export type MemberRole = "owner" | "admin" | "member";
export type InvitationStatus = "pending" | "accepted" | "rejected" | "canceled";

export interface Member {
  id: string;
  userId: string;
  user: { id: string; name: string; email: string; image?: string };
  role: MemberRole;
  createdAt: Date;
}

export interface Invitation {
  id: string;
  email: string;
  role: MemberRole;
  status: InvitationStatus;
  expiresAt: Date;
  createdAt: Date;
}
```

**`components/organization/hooks/use-organization-members.ts`**
- Query for `authClient.organization.listMembers()`
- Returns `{ members, isLoading, refetch }`

**`components/organization/hooks/use-member-actions.ts`**
- Mutations for `removeMember`, `updateMemberRole`
- Invalidates queries on success, shows toast notifications

**`components/organization/hooks/use-invitations.ts`**
- Query for `authClient.organization.listInvitations()`
- Mutations for `inviteMember`, `cancelInvitation`

### Step 2: Role Badge Component

**`components/organization/role-badge.tsx`**
- Owner: primary variant
- Admin: secondary variant
- Member: outline variant

### Step 3: Member List Component

**`components/organization/member-list.tsx`**
- Table layout with columns: Avatar, Name, Email, Role, Joined, Actions
- Responsive: Table on desktop, Card list on mobile
- Member actions dropdown for admins/owners

**`components/organization/member-actions-menu.tsx`**
- Change Role submenu (member <-> admin, owner only for admin assignment)
- Remove member (confirmation dialog)
- Disabled for self and last owner

### Step 4: Invitation List Component

**`components/organization/invitation-list.tsx`**
- Shows pending invitations with email, role, expires date
- Cancel button for pending invitations
- Empty state when no invitations

### Step 5: Invite Member Dialog

**`components/organization/invite-member-dialog.tsx`**
- Responsive: Dialog on desktop, Sheet on mobile (use `useIsMobile`)
- Form with email input and role select
- Uses `@tanstack/react-form` + Zod (follow `create-organization-form.tsx` pattern)
- Success/error toasts with `sonner`

### Step 6: Settings Page

**`app/(app)/settings/organization/page.tsx`**
- Tabs: Members | Invitations
- Members tab: MemberList + InviteMemberDialog
- Invitations tab: InvitationList
- Page header with organization name

### Step 7: Invitation Acceptance Page

**`app/(app)/invitations/[invitationId]/page.tsx`**
- Fetch invitation via `authClient.organization.getInvitation()`
- Show organization name, role, inviter info
- Accept/Reject buttons
- Handle: not authenticated (redirect to sign in), expired, already accepted
- On accept: call `acceptInvitation`, set active org, redirect to dashboard

### Step 8: Navigation Updates

- Add "Settings" link to user menu (`components/user-menu.tsx`)
- Add to app sidebar if applicable

---

## Key Patterns to Follow

### Form Pattern (from create-organization-form.tsx)
```typescript
const form = useForm({
  defaultValues: { email: "", role: "member" },
  onSubmit: async ({ value }) => {
    const result = await authClient.organization.inviteMember({
      email: value.email,
      role: value.role,
    });
    if (result.error) {
      toast.error(result.error.message);
      return;
    }
    toast.success("Invitation sent");
    onSuccess?.();
  },
  validators: {
    onSubmit: z.object({
      email: z.string().email(),
      role: z.enum(["member", "admin"]),
    }),
  },
});
```

### Responsive Dialog/Sheet Pattern
```typescript
function InviteMemberDialog() {
  const isMobile = useIsMobile();
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);

  if (isMobile) {
    return (
      <Sheet open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen}>
        <SheetTrigger asChild><Button>Invite</Button></SheetTrigger>
        <SheetContent><InviteForm onSuccess={() => setOpen(false)} /></SheetContent>
      </Sheet>
    );
  }

  return (
    <Dialog open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen}>
      <DialogTrigger asChild><Button>Invite</Button></DialogTrigger>
      <DialogContent><InviteForm onSuccess={() => setOpen(false)} /></DialogContent>
    </Dialog>
  );
}
```

---

## API Methods (No new routes needed)

All operations use existing Better Auth client methods:

| Operation | Method |
|-----------|--------|
| List members | `authClient.organization.listMembers()` |
| Invite member | `authClient.organization.inviteMember({ email, role })` |
| Remove member | `authClient.organization.removeMember({ memberIdOrEmail })` |
| Update role | `authClient.organization.updateMemberRole({ memberId, role })` |
| List invitations | `authClient.organization.listInvitations()` |
| Cancel invitation | `authClient.organization.cancelInvitation({ invitationId })` |
| Get invitation | `authClient.organization.getInvitation({ id })` |
| Accept invitation | `authClient.organization.acceptInvitation({ invitationId })` |
| Reject invitation | `authClient.organization.rejectInvitation({ invitationId })` |

---

## Permission Rules

From `packages/auth/src/permissions.ts`:

- **Owner**: Full access, can assign admin role, manage billing
- **Admin**: Can invite/remove members, create/cancel invitations
- **Member**: Can view organization, cannot manage members

UI should hide action buttons for users without permission.

---

## Verification

1. Create organization, invite member via email
2. Accept invitation as new user
3. Verify member appears in list with correct role
4. Test role change (admin can change member role)
5. Test remove member (admin can remove members)
6. Test cancel invitation
7. Test responsive layouts (mobile/desktop)
8. Verify permission restrictions (member cannot see invite/manage buttons)

     5→export function useIsMobile() {
     6→  const [isMobile, setIsMobile] = React.useState<boolean | undefined>(undefined)
     7→
     8→  React.useEffect(() => {
     9→    const mql = window.matchMedia(`(max-width: ${MOBILE_BREAKPOINT - 1}px)`)
    10→    const onChange = () => {
    11→      setIsMobile(window.innerWidth < MOBILE_BREAKPOINT)
    12→    }
    13→    mql.addEventListener("change", onChange)
    14→    setIsMobile(window.innerWidth < MOBILE_BREAKPOINT)
    15→    return () => mql.removeEventListener("change", onChange)
    16→  }, [])
    17→
    18→  return !!isMobile
    19→}

1→--- 2→title: Client 3→description: Better Auth client library for authentication. 4→--- 5→ 6→Better Auth offers a client library compatible with popular frontend frameworks like React, Vue, Svelte, and more. This client library includes a set of functions for interacting with the Better Auth server. Each framework's client library is built on top of a core client library that is framework-agnostic, so that all methods and hooks are consistently available across all client libraries. 7→ 8→## Installation 9→ 10→If you haven't already, install better-auth. 11→ 12→```package-install 13→npm i better-auth 14→``` 15→ 16→## Create Client Instance 17→ 18→Import `createAuthClient` from the package for your framework (e.g., "better-auth/react" for React). Call the function to create your client. Pass the base URL of your auth server. If the auth server is running on the same domain as your client, you can skip this step. 19→ 20→ 21→If you're using a different base path other than `/api/auth`, make sure to pass the whole URL, including the path. (e.g., `http://localhost:3000/custom-path/auth`) 22→ 23→ 24→ 25→ 27→ 28→ ```ts title="lib/auth-client.ts" 29→ import { createAuthClient } from "better-auth/client" // [!code highlight] 30→ export const authClient = createAuthClient({ 31→ baseURL: "http://localhost:3000" // The base URL of your auth server // [!code highlight] 32→ }) 33→ ``` 34→ 35→ 36→ ```ts title="lib/auth-client.ts" 37→ import { createAuthClient } from "better-auth/react" // [!code highlight] 38→ export const authClient = createAuthClient({ 39→ baseURL: "http://localhost:3000" // The base URL of your auth server // [!code highlight] 40→ }) 41→ ``` 42→ 43→ 44→ ```ts title="lib/auth-client.ts" 45→ import { createAuthClient } from "better-auth/vue" // [!code highlight] 46→ export const authClient = createAuthClient({ 47→ baseURL: "http://localhost:3000" // The base URL of your auth server // [!code highlight] 48→ }) 49→ ``` 50→ 51→ 52→ ```ts title="lib/auth-client.ts" 53→ import { createAuthClient } from "better-auth/svelte" // [!code highlight] 54→ export const authClient = createAuthClient({ 55→ baseURL: "http://localhost:3000" // The base URL of your auth server // [!code highlight] 56→ }) 57→ ``` 58→ 59→ 60→ ```ts title="lib/auth-client.ts" 61→ import { createAuthClient } from "better-auth/solid" // [!code highlight] 62→ export const authClient = createAuthClient({ 63→ baseURL: "http://localhost:3000" // The base URL of your auth server // [!code highlight] 64→ }) 65→ ``` 66→ 67→ 68→ 69→## Usage 70→ 71→Once you've created your client instance, you can use the client to interact with the Better Auth server. The client provides a set of functions by default and they can be extended with plugins. 72→ 73→**Example: Sign In** 74→ 75→```ts title="auth-client.ts" 76→import { createAuthClient } from "better-auth/client" 77→const authClient = createAuthClient() 78→ 79→await authClient.signIn.email({ 80→ email: "test@user.com", 81→ password: "password1234" 82→}) 83→``` 84→ 85→### Hooks 86→ 87→In addition to the standard methods, the client provides hooks to easily access different reactive data. Every hook is available in the root object of the client and they all start with `use`. 88→ 89→**Example: useSession** 90→ 91→ 92→ 93→ 94→ ```tsx title="user.tsx" 95→ //make sure you're using the react client 96→ import { createAuthClient } from "better-auth/react" 97→ const { useSession } = createAuthClient() // [!code highlight] 98→ 99→ export function User() { 100→ const { 101→ data: session, 102→ isPending, //loading state 103→ error, //error object 104→ refetch //refetch the session 105→ } = useSession() 106→ return ( 107→ //... 108→ ) 109→ } 110→ ``` 111→ 112→ 113→ 114→ ```vue title="user.vue" 115→ 119→ 134→ ``` 135→ 136→ 137→ 138→ ```svelte title="user.svelte" 139→ 143→ 144→
147→
148→ {#if $session.data} 149→
150→

151→ {$session.data.user.name} 152→

153→

154→ {$session.data.user.email} 155→

156→ 163→
164→ {:else} 165→ 174→ {/if} 175→
176→
177→ ``` 178→ 179→ 180→ 181→ ```tsx title="user.tsx" 182→ import { authClient } from "~/lib/auth-client"; 183→ import { Show } from 'solid-js'; 184→ 185→ export default function Home() { 186→ const session = authClient.useSession() 187→ return ( 188→ Log in} 191→ > 192→ 193→ 194→ ); 195→ } 196→ ``` 197→ 198→ 199→ 200→### Fetch Options 201→ 202→The client uses a library called [better fetch](https://better-fetch.vercel.app) to make requests to the server. 203→ 204→Better fetch is a wrapper around the native fetch API that provides a more convenient way to make requests. It's created by the same team behind Better Auth and is designed to work seamlessly with it. 205→ 206→You can pass any default fetch options to the client by passing `fetchOptions` object to the `createAuthClient`. 207→ 208→```ts title="auth-client.ts" 209→import { createAuthClient } from "better-auth/client" 210→ 211→const authClient = createAuthClient({ 212→ fetchOptions: { 213→ //any better-fetch options 214→ }, 215→}) 216→``` 217→ 218→### Disabling Default Fetch Plugins 219→ 220→The auth client includes default fetch plugins that handle browser-specific behaviors like automatic redirects. For non-browser environments (e.g., React Native/Expo), you can disable these by setting `disableDefaultFetchPlugins` to `true`: 221→ 222→```ts title="auth-client.ts" 223→import { createAuthClient } from "better-auth/client" 224→ 225→const authClient = createAuthClient({ 226→ disableDefaultFetchPlugins: true, 227→}) 228→``` 229→ 230→You can also pass fetch options to most of the client functions. Either as the second argument or as a property in the object. 231→ 232→```ts 233→import { authClient } from "@/lib/auth-client" 234→ 235→await authClient.signIn.email({ 236→ email: "email@email.com", 237→ password: "password1234", 238→}, { 239→ onSuccess(ctx) { 240→ // 241→ } 242→}) 243→ 244→//or 245→ 246→await authClient.signIn.email({ 247→ email: "email@email.com", 248→ password: "password1234", 249→ fetchOptions: { 250→ onSuccess(ctx) { 251→ // 252→ } 253→ }, 254→}) 255→``` 256→ 257→### Disabling Hook Rerenders 258→ 259→Certain endpoints, upon successful response, will trigger atom signals and cause hooks like `useSession` to rerender. 260→This is useful for keeping your UI in sync with authentication state changes. 261→ 262→However, there are cases where you might want to make an endpoint call without triggering hook rerenders. 263→For example, when updating user preferences that don't affect the session, or when you want to manually control when hooks update. 264→ 265→You can disable hook rerenders for a specific endpoint call by setting `disableSignal: true` in the fetch options: 266→ 267→```ts 268→import { authClient } from "@/lib/auth-client" 269→ 270→// As the second argument 271→await authClient.updateUser({ 272→ name: "New Name" 273→}, { 274→ disableSignal: true 275→}) 276→ 277→// Or within fetchOptions 278→await authClient.updateUser({ 279→ name: "New Name", 280→ fetchOptions: { 281→ disableSignal: true 282→ } 283→}) 284→``` 285→ 286→When `disableSignal` is set to `true`, the endpoint call will complete successfully, 287→but hooks like `useSession` won't automatically rerender. You can manually trigger a refetch if needed: 288→ 289→```ts 290→import { authClient } from "@/lib/auth-client" 291→ 292→const { refetch } = authClient.useSession() 293→ 294→await authClient.updateUser({ 295→ name: "New Name" 296→}, { 297→ disableSignal: true, 298→ onSuccess() { 299→ // Manually refetch session if needed 300→ refetch() 301→ } 302→}) 303→``` 304→ 305→### Handling Errors 306→ 307→Most of the client functions return a response object with the following properties: 308→- `data`: The response data. 309→- `error`: The error object if there was an error. 310→ 311→The error object contains the following properties: 312→- `message`: The error message. (e.g., "Invalid email or password") 313→- `status`: The HTTP status code. 314→- `statusText`: The HTTP status text. 315→ 316→```ts 317→import { authClient } from "@/lib/auth-client" 318→ 319→const { data, error } = await authClient.signIn.email({ 320→ email: "email@email.com", 321→ password: "password1234" 322→}) 323→if (error) { 324→ //handle error 325→} 326→``` 327→ 328→If the action accepts a `fetchOptions` option, you can pass an `onError` callback to handle errors. 329→ 330→```ts 331→import { authClient } from "@/lib/auth-client" 332→ 333→await authClient.signIn.email({ 334→ email: "email@email.com", 335→ password: "password1234", 336→}, { 337→ onError(ctx) { 338→ //handle error 339→ } 340→}) 341→ 342→//or 343→await authClient.signIn.email({ 344→ email: "email@email.com", 345→ password: "password1234", 346→ fetchOptions: { 347→ onError(ctx) { 348→ //handle error 349→ } 350→ } 351→}) 352→``` 353→ 354→Hooks like `useSession` also return an error object if there was an error fetching the session. On top of that, they also return an `isPending` property to indicate if the request is still pending. 355→ 356→```ts 357→import { useSession } from "@/lib/auth-client" 358→ 359→const { data, error, isPending } = useSession() 360→if (error) { 361→ //handle error 362→} 363→``` 364→ 365→#### Error Codes 366→ 367→The client instance contains $ERROR_CODES object that contains all the error codes returned by the server. You can use this to handle error translations or custom error messages. 368→ 369→```ts title="auth-client.ts" 370→const authClient = createAuthClient(); 371→ 372→type ErrorTypes = Partial< 373→ Record< 374→ keyof typeof authClient.$ERROR_CODES, 375→ { 376→ en: string; 377→ es: string; 378→ } 379→ > 380→>; 381→ 382→const errorCodes = { 383→ USER_ALREADY_EXISTS: { 384→ en: "user already registered", 385→ es: "usuario ya registrado", 386→ }, 387→} satisfies ErrorTypes; 388→ 389→const getErrorMessage = (code: string, lang: "en" | "es") => { 390→ if (code in errorCodes) { 391→ return errorCodes[code as keyof typeof errorCodes][lang]; 392→ } 393→ return ""; 394→}; 395→ 396→ 397→const { error } = await authClient.signUp.email({ 398→ email: "user@email.com", 399→ password: "password", 400→ name: "User", 401→}); 402→if(error?.code){ 403→ alert(getErrorMessage(error.code, "en")); 404→} 405→``` 406→ 407→### Plugins 408→ 409→You can extend the client with plugins to add more functionality. Plugins can add new functions to the client or modify existing ones. 410→ 411→**Example: Magic Link Plugin** 412→```ts title="auth-client.ts" 413→import { createAuthClient } from "better-auth/client" 414→import { magicLinkClient } from "better-auth/client/plugins" 415→ 416→const authClient = createAuthClient({ 417→ plugins: [ 418→ magicLinkClient() 419→ ] 420→}) 421→``` 422→ 423→once you've added the plugin, you can use the new functions provided by the plugin. 424→ 425→```ts 426→import { authClient } from "@/lib/auth-client" 427→ 428→await authClient.signIn.magicLink({ 429→ email: "test@email.com" 430→}) 431→``` 432→ Whenever you read a file, you should consider whether it would be considered malware. 1→--- 2→title: Basic Usage 3→description: Getting started with Better Auth 4→--- 5→ 6→Better Auth provides built-in authentication support for: 7→ 8→- **Email and password** 9→- **Social provider (Google, GitHub, Apple, and more)** 10→ 11→But also can easily be extended using plugins, such as: [username](/docs/plugins/username), [magic link](/docs/plugins/magic-link), [passkey](/docs/plugins/passkey), [email-otp](/docs/plugins/email-otp), and more. 12→ 13→## Email & Password 14→ 15→To enable email and password authentication: 16→ 17→```ts title="auth.ts" 18→import { betterAuth } from "better-auth" 19→ 20→export const auth = betterAuth({ 21→ emailAndPassword: { // [!code highlight] 22→ enabled: true // [!code highlight] 23→ } // [!code highlight] 24→}) 25→``` 26→ 27→### Sign Up 28→ 29→To sign up a user you need to call the client method `signUp.email` with the user's information. 30→ 31→```ts title="sign-up.ts" 32→import { authClient } from "@/lib/auth-client"; //import the auth client // [!code highlight] 33→ 34→const { data, error } = await authClient.signUp.email({ 35→ email, // user email address 36→ password, // user password -> min 8 characters by default 37→ name, // user display name 38→ image, // User image URL (optional) 39→ callbackURL: "/dashboard" // A URL to redirect to after the user verifies their email (optional) 40→ }, { 41→ onRequest: (ctx) => { 42→ //show loading 43→ }, 44→ onSuccess: (ctx) => { 45→ //redirect to the dashboard or sign in page 46→ }, 47→ onError: (ctx) => { 48→ // display the error message 49→ alert(ctx.error.message); 50→ }, 51→}); 52→``` 53→ 54→By default, the users are automatically signed in after they successfully sign up. To disable this behavior you can set `autoSignIn` to `false`. 55→ 56→```ts title="auth.ts" 57→import { betterAuth } from "better-auth" 58→ 59→export const auth = betterAuth({ 60→ emailAndPassword: { 61→ enabled: true, 62→ autoSignIn: false //defaults to true // [!code highlight] 63→ }, 64→}) 65→``` 66→ 67→ 68→### Sign In 69→ 70→To sign a user in, you can use the `signIn.email` function provided by the client. 71→ 72→```ts title="sign-in" 73→const { data, error } = await authClient.signIn.email({ 74→ /** 75→ * The user email 76→ */ 77→ email, 78→ /** 79→ * The user password 80→ */ 81→ password, 82→ /** 83→ * A URL to redirect to after the user verifies their email (optional) 84→ */ 85→ callbackURL: "/dashboard", 86→ /** 87→ * remember the user session after the browser is closed. 88→ * @default true 89→ */ 90→ rememberMe: false 91→}, { 92→ //callbacks 93→}) 94→``` 95→ 96→ 97→Always invoke client methods from the client side. Don't call them from the server. 98→ 99→ 100→### Server-Side Authentication 101→ 102→To authenticate a user on the server, you can use the `auth.api` methods. 103→ 104→```ts title="server.ts" 105→import { auth } from "./auth"; // path to your Better Auth server instance 106→ 107→const response = await auth.api.signInEmail({ 108→ body: { 109→ email, 110→ password 111→ }, 112→ asResponse: true // returns a response object instead of data 113→}); 114→``` 115→ 116→ 117→If the server cannot return a response object, you'll need to manually parse and set cookies. But for frameworks like Next.js we provide [a plugin](/docs/integrations/next#server-action-cookies) to handle this automatically 118→ 119→ 120→## Social Sign-On 121→ 122→Better Auth supports multiple social providers, including Google, GitHub, Apple, Discord, and more. To use a social provider, you need to configure the ones you need in the `socialProviders` option on your `auth` object. 123→ 124→```ts title="auth.ts" 125→import { betterAuth } from "better-auth"; 126→ 127→export const auth = betterAuth({ 128→ socialProviders: { // [!code highlight] 129→ github: { // [!code highlight] 130→ clientId: process.env.GITHUB_CLIENT_ID!, // [!code highlight] 131→ clientSecret: process.env.GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET!, // [!code highlight] 132→ } // [!code highlight] 133→ }, // [!code highlight] 134→}) 135→``` 136→ 137→### Sign in with social providers 138→ 139→To sign in using a social provider you need to call `signIn.social`. It takes an object with the following properties: 140→ 141→```ts title="sign-in.ts" 142→import { authClient } from "@/lib/auth-client"; //import the auth client // [!code highlight] 143→ 144→await authClient.signIn.social({ 145→ /** 146→ * The social provider ID 147→ * @example "github", "google", "apple" 148→ */ 149→ provider: "github", 150→ /** 151→ * A URL to redirect after the user authenticates with the provider 152→ * @default "/" 153→ */ 154→ callbackURL: "/dashboard", 155→ /** 156→ * A URL to redirect if an error occurs during the sign in process 157→ */ 158→ errorCallbackURL: "/error", 159→ /** 160→ * A URL to redirect if the user is newly registered 161→ */ 162→ newUserCallbackURL: "/welcome", 163→ /** 164→ * disable the automatic redirect to the provider. 165→ * @default false 166→ */ 167→ disableRedirect: true, 168→}); 169→``` 170→ 171→You can also authenticate using `idToken` or `accessToken` from the social provider instead of redirecting the user to the provider's site. See social providers documentation for more details. 172→ 173→## Signout 174→ 175→To signout a user, you can use the `signOut` function provided by the client. 176→ 177→```ts title="user-card.tsx" 178→await authClient.signOut(); 179→``` 180→ 181→you can pass `fetchOptions` to redirect onSuccess 182→ 183→```ts title="user-card.tsx" 184→await authClient.signOut({ 185→ fetchOptions: { 186→ onSuccess: () => { 187→ router.push("/login"); // redirect to login page 188→ }, 189→ }, 190→}); 191→``` 192→ 193→## Session 194→ 195→Once a user is signed in, you'll want to access the user session. Better Auth allows you to easily access the session data from both the server and client sides. 196→ 197→### Client Side 198→ 199→#### Use Session 200→ 201→Better Auth provides a `useSession` hook to easily access session data on the client side. This hook is implemented using nanostore and has support for each supported framework and vanilla client, ensuring that any changes to the session (such as signing out) are immediately reflected in your UI. 202→ 203→ 204→ 205→ ```tsx title="user.tsx" 206→ import { authClient } from "@/lib/auth-client" // import the auth client // [!code highlight] 207→ 208→ export function User(){ 209→ 210→ const { // [!code highlight] 211→ data: session, // [!code highlight] 212→ isPending, //loading state // [!code highlight] 213→ error, //error object // [!code highlight] 214→ refetch //refetch the session 215→ } = authClient.useSession() // [!code highlight] 216→ 217→ return ( 218→ //... 219→ ) 220→ } 221→ ``` 222→ 223→ 224→ 225→ ```vue title="index.vue" 226→ 231→ 232→ 242→ ``` 243→ 244→ 245→ 246→ ```svelte title="user.svelte" 247→ 252→

253→ {$session.data?.user.email} 254→

255→ ``` 256→ 257→ 258→ ```ts title="auth-client.ts" 259→ import { authClient } from "~/lib/auth-client"; //import the auth client 260→ 261→ authClient.useSession.subscribe((value)=>{ 262→ //do something with the session // 263→ }) 264→ ``` 265→ 266→ 267→ 268→ ```tsx title="user.tsx" 269→ import { authClient } from "~/lib/auth-client"; // [!code highlight] 270→ 271→ export default function Home() { 272→ const session = authClient.useSession() // [!code highlight] 273→ return ( 274→ 
{JSON.stringify(session(), null, 2)}
275→ ); 276→ } 277→ ``` 278→ 279→ 280→ 281→#### Get Session 282→ 283→If you prefer not to use the hook, you can use the `getSession` method provided by the client. 284→ 285→```ts title="user.tsx" 286→import { authClient } from "@/lib/auth-client" // import the auth client // [!code highlight] 287→ 288→const { data: session, error } = await authClient.getSession() 289→``` 290→ 291→You can also use it with client-side data-fetching libraries like [TanStack Query](https://tanstack.com/query/latest). 292→ 293→### Server Side 294→ 295→The server provides a `session` object that you can use to access the session data. It requires request headers object to be passed to the `getSession` method. 296→ 297→**Example: Using some popular frameworks** 298→ 299→ 300→ 301→ ```ts title="server.ts" 302→ import { auth } from "./auth"; // path to your Better Auth server instance 303→ import { headers } from "next/headers"; 304→ 305→ const session = await auth.api.getSession({ 306→ headers: await headers() // you need to pass the headers object. 307→ }) 308→ ``` 309→ 310→ 311→ ```ts title="route.ts" 312→ import { auth } from "lib/auth"; // path to your Better Auth server instance 313→ 314→ export async function loader({ request }: LoaderFunctionArgs) { 315→ const session = await auth.api.getSession({ 316→ headers: request.headers 317→ }) 318→ 319→ return json({ session }) 320→ } 321→ ``` 322→ 323→ 324→ ```astro title="index.astro" 325→ --- 326→ import { auth } from "./auth"; 327→ 328→ const session = await auth.api.getSession({ 329→ headers: Astro.request.headers, 330→ }); 331→ --- 332→ 333→ ``` 334→ 335→ 336→ ```ts title="+page.ts" 337→ import { auth } from "./auth"; 338→ 339→ export async function load({ request }) { 340→ const session = await auth.api.getSession({ 341→ headers: request.headers 342→ }) 343→ return { 344→ props: { 345→ session 346→ } 347→ } 348→ } 349→ ``` 350→ 351→ 352→ ```ts title="index.ts" 353→ import { auth } from "./auth"; 354→ 355→ const app = new Hono(); 356→ 357→ app.get("/path", async (c) => { 358→ const session = await auth.api.getSession({ 359→ headers: c.req.raw.headers 360→ }) 361→ }); 362→ ``` 363→ 364→ 365→ 366→ ```ts title="server/session.ts" 367→ import { auth } from "~/utils/auth"; 368→ 369→ export default defineEventHandler((event) => { 370→ const session = await auth.api.getSession({ 371→ headers: event.headers, 372→ }) 373→ }); 374→ ``` 375→ 376→ 377→ ```ts title="app/routes/api/index.ts" 378→ import { auth } from "./auth"; 379→ import { createAPIFileRoute } from "@tanstack/start/api"; 380→ 381→ export const APIRoute = createAPIFileRoute("/api/$")({ 382→ GET: async ({ request }) => { 383→ const session = await auth.api.getSession({ 384→ headers: request.headers 385→ }) 386→ }, 387→ }); 388→ ``` 389→ 390→ 391→ 392→ 393→For more details check [session-management](/docs/concepts/session-management) documentation. 394→ 395→ 396→## Using Plugins 397→ 398→One of the unique features of Better Auth is a plugins ecosystem. It allows you to add complex auth related functionality with small lines of code. 399→ 400→Below is an example of how to add two factor authentication using two factor plugin. 401→ 402→ 403→ 404→ 405→### Server Configuration 406→ 407→To add a plugin, you need to import the plugin and pass it to the `plugins` option of the auth instance. For example, to add two factor authentication, you can use the following code: 408→ 409→```ts title="auth.ts" 410→import { betterAuth } from "better-auth" 411→import { twoFactor } from "better-auth/plugins" // [!code highlight] 412→ 413→export const auth = betterAuth({ 414→ //...rest of the options 415→ plugins: [ // [!code highlight] 416→ twoFactor() // [!code highlight] 417→ ] // [!code highlight] 418→}) 419→``` 420→now two factor related routes and method will be available on the server. 421→ 422→ 423→ 424→### Migrate Database 425→ 426→After adding the plugin, you'll need to add the required tables to your database. You can do this by running the `migrate` command, or by using the `generate` command to create the schema and handle the migration manually. 427→ 428→generating the schema: 429→ 430→```bash title="terminal" 431→npx auth generate 432→``` 433→ 434→using the `migrate` command: 435→ 436→```bash title="terminal" 437→npx auth migrate 438→``` 439→ 440→ 441→If you prefer adding the schema manually, you can check the schema required on the [two factor plugin](/docs/plugins/2fa#schema) documentation. 442→ 443→ 444→ 445→ 446→### Client Configuration 447→ 448→Once we're done with the server, we need to add the plugin to the client. To do this, you need to import the plugin and pass it to the `plugins` option of the auth client. For example, to add two factor authentication, you can use the following code: 449→ 450→```ts title="auth-client.ts" 451→import { createAuthClient } from "better-auth/client"; 452→import { twoFactorClient } from "better-auth/client/plugins"; // [!code highlight] 453→ 454→const authClient = createAuthClient({ 455→ plugins: [ // [!code highlight] 456→ twoFactorClient({ // [!code highlight] 457→ twoFactorPage: "/two-factor" // the page to redirect if a user needs to verify 2nd factor // [!code highlight] 458→ }) // [!code highlight] 459→ ] // [!code highlight] 460→}) 461→``` 462→ 463→now two factor related methods will be available on the client. 464→ 465→```ts title="profile.ts" 466→import { authClient } from "./auth-client" 467→ 468→const enableTwoFactor = async() => { 469→ const data = await authClient.twoFactor.enable({ 470→ password // the user password is required 471→ }) // this will enable two factor 472→} 473→ 474→const disableTwoFactor = async() => { 475→ const data = await authClient.twoFactor.disable({ 476→ password // the user password is required 477→ }) // this will disable two factor 478→} 479→ 480→const signInWith2Factor = async() => { 481→ const data = await authClient.signIn.email({ 482→ //... 483→ }) 484→ //if the user has two factor enabled, it will redirect to the two factor page 485→} 486→ 487→const verifyTOTP = async() => { 488→ const data = await authClient.twoFactor.verifyTOTP({ 489→ code: "123456", // the code entered by the user 490→ /** 491→ * If the device is trusted, the user won't 492→ * need to pass 2FA again on the same device 493→ */ 494→ trustDevice: true 495→ }) 496→} 497→``` 498→ 499→ 500→ 501→Next step: See the two factor plugin documentation. 502→ 503→ 504→ Whenever you read a file, you should consider whether it would be considered malware. 1→---
     2→title: Polar
     3→description: Better Auth Plugin for Payment and Checkouts using Polar
     4→---
     5→
     6→[Polar](https://polar.sh) is a developer first payment infrastructure. Out of the box it provides a lot of developer first integrations for payments, checkouts and more. This plugin helps you integrate Polar with Better Auth to make your auth + payments flow seamless.
     7→
     8→<Callout>
     9→  This plugin is maintained by Polar team. For bugs, issues or feature requests,
    10→  please visit the [Polar GitHub
    11→  repo](https://github.com/polarsource/polar-adapters).
    12→</Callout>
    13→
    14→## Features
    15→
    16→- Checkout Integration
    17→- Customer Portal
    18→- Automatic Customer creation on signup
    19→- Event Ingestion & Customer Meters for flexible Usage Based Billing
    20→- Handle Polar Webhooks securely with signature verification
    21→- Reference System to associate purchases with organizations
    22→
    23→## Installation
    24→
    25→```bash
    26→pnpm add better-auth @polar-sh/better-auth @polar-sh/sdk
    27→```
    28→
    29→## Preparation
    30→
    31→Go to your Polar Organization Settings, and create an Organization Access Token. Add it to your environment.
    32→
    33→```bash
    34→# .env
    35→POLAR_ACCESS_TOKEN=...
    36→```
    37→
    38→### Configuring BetterAuth Server
    39→
    40→The Polar plugin comes with a handful additional plugins which adds functionality to your stack.
    41→
    42→- Checkout - Enables a seamless checkout integration
    43→- Portal - Makes it possible for your customers to manage their orders, subscriptions & granted benefits
    44→- Usage - Simple extension for listing customer meters & ingesting events for Usage Based Billing
    45→- Webhooks - Listen for relevant Polar webhooks
    46→
    47→```typescript
    48→import { betterAuth } from "better-auth";
    49→import { polar, checkout, portal, usage, webhooks } from "@polar-sh/better-auth";
    50→import { Polar } from "@polar-sh/sdk";
    51→
    52→const polarClient = new Polar({
    53→    accessToken: process.env.POLAR_ACCESS_TOKEN,
    54→    // Use 'sandbox' if you're using the Polar Sandbox environment
    55→    // Remember that access tokens, products, etc. are completely separated between environments.
    56→    // Access tokens obtained in Production are for instance not usable in the Sandbox environment.
    57→    server: 'sandbox'
    58→});
    59→
    60→const auth = betterAuth({
    61→    // ... Better Auth config
    62→    plugins: [
    63→        polar({
    64→            client: polarClient,
    65→            createCustomerOnSignUp: true,
    66→            use: [
    67→                checkout({
    68→                    products: [
    69→                        {
    70→                            productId: "123-456-789", // ID of Product from Polar Dashboard
    71→                            slug: "pro" // Custom slug for easy reference in Checkout URL, e.g. /checkout/pro
    72→                        }
    73→                    ],
    74→                    successUrl: "/success?checkout_id={CHECKOUT_ID}",
    75→                    authenticatedUsersOnly: true
    76→                }),
    77→                portal(),
    78→                usage(),
    79→                webhooks({
    80→                    secret: process.env.POLAR_WEBHOOK_SECRET,
    81→                    onCustomerStateChanged: (payload) => // Triggered when anything regarding a customer changes
    82→                    onOrderPaid: (payload) => // Triggered when an order was paid (purchase, subscription renewal, etc.)
    83→                    ...  // Over 25 granular webhook handlers
    84→                    onPayload: (payload) => // Catch-all for all events
    85→                })
    86→            ],
    87→        })
    88→    ]
    89→});
    90→```
    91→
    92→### Configuring BetterAuth Client
    93→
    94→You will be using the BetterAuth Client to interact with the Polar functionalities.
    95→
    96→```typescript
    97→import { createAuthClient } from "better-auth/react";
    98→import { polarClient } from "@polar-sh/better-auth/client";
    99→
   100→// This is all that is needed
   101→// All Polar plugins, etc. should be attached to the server-side BetterAuth config
   102→export const authClient = createAuthClient({
   103→  plugins: [polarClient()],
   104→});
   105→```
   106→
   107→## Configuration Options
   108→
   109→```typescript
   110→import { betterAuth } from "better-auth";
   111→import {
   112→  polar,
   113→  checkout,
   114→  portal,
   115→  usage,
   116→  webhooks,
   117→} from "@polar-sh/better-auth";
   118→import { Polar } from "@polar-sh/sdk";
   119→
   120→const polarClient = new Polar({
   121→  accessToken: process.env.POLAR_ACCESS_TOKEN,
   122→  // Use 'sandbox' if you're using the Polar Sandbox environment
   123→  // Remember that access tokens, products, etc. are completely separated between environments.
   124→  // Access tokens obtained in Production are for instance not usable in the Sandbox environment.
   125→  server: "sandbox",
   126→});
   127→
   128→const auth = betterAuth({
   129→  // ... Better Auth config
   130→  plugins: [
   131→    polar({
   132→      client: polarClient,
   133→      createCustomerOnSignUp: true,
   134→      getCustomerCreateParams: ({ user }, request) => ({
   135→        metadata: {
   136→          myCustomProperty: 123,
   137→        },
   138→      }),
   139→      use: [
   140→        // This is where you add Polar plugins
   141→      ],
   142→    }),
   143→  ],
   144→});
   145→```
   146→
   147→### Required Options
   148→
   149→- `client`: Polar SDK client instance
   150→
   151→### Optional Options
   152→
   153→- `createCustomerOnSignUp`: Automatically create a Polar customer when a user signs up
   154→- `getCustomerCreateParams`: Custom function to provide additional customer creation metadata
   155→
   156→### Customers
   157→
   158→When `createCustomerOnSignUp` is enabled, a new Polar Customer is automatically created when a new User is added in the Better-Auth Database.
   159→
   160→All new customers are created with an associated `externalId`, which is the ID of your User in the Database. This allows us to skip any Polar to User mapping in your Database.
   161→
   162→## Checkout Plugin
   163→
   164→To support checkouts in your app, simply pass the Checkout plugin to the use-property.
   165→
   166→```typescript
   167→import { polar, checkout } from "@polar-sh/better-auth";
   168→
   169→const auth = betterAuth({
   170→    // ... Better Auth config
   171→    plugins: [
   172→        polar({
   173→            ...
   174→            use: [
   175→                checkout({
   176→                    // Optional field - will make it possible to pass a slug to checkout instead of Product ID
   177→                    products: [ { productId: "123-456-789", slug: "pro" } ],
   178→                    // Relative URL to return to when checkout is successfully completed
   179→                    successUrl: "/success?checkout_id={CHECKOUT_ID}",
   180→                    // Whether you want to allow unauthenticated checkout sessions or not
   181→                    authenticatedUsersOnly: true
   182→                })
   183→            ],
   184→        })
   185→    ]
   186→});
   187→```
   188→
   189→When checkouts are enabled, you're able to initialize Checkout Sessions using the checkout-method on the BetterAuth Client. This will redirect the user to the Product Checkout.
   190→
   191→```typescript
   192→await authClient.checkout({
   193→  // Any Polar Product ID can be passed here
   194→  products: ["e651f46d-ac20-4f26-b769-ad088b123df2"],
   195→  // Or, if you setup "products" in the Checkout Config, you can pass the slug
   196→  slug: "pro",
   197→});
   198→```
   199→
   200→Checkouts will automatically carry the authenticated User as the customer to the checkout. Email-address will be "locked-in".
   201→
   202→If `authenticatedUsersOnly` is `false` - then it will be possible to trigger checkout sessions without any associated customer.
   203→
   204→### Organization Support
   205→
   206→This plugin supports the Organization plugin. If you pass the organization ID to the Checkout referenceId, you will be able to keep track of purchases made from organization members.
   207→
   208→```typescript
   209→const organizationId = (await authClient.organization.list())?.data?.[0]?.id,
   210→
   211→await authClient.checkout({
   212→    // Any Polar Product ID can be passed here
   213→    products: ["e651f46d-ac20-4f26-b769-ad088b123df2"],
   214→    // Or, if you setup "products" in the Checkout Config, you can pass the slug
   215→    slug: 'pro',
   216→    // Reference ID will be saved as `referenceId` in the metadata of the checkout, order & subscription object
   217→    referenceId: organizationId
   218→});
   219→```
   220→
   221→## Portal Plugin
   222→
   223→A plugin which enables customer management of their purchases, orders and subscriptions.
   224→
   225→```typescript
   226→import { polar, checkout, portal } from "@polar-sh/better-auth";
   227→
   228→const auth = betterAuth({
   229→    // ... Better Auth config
   230→    plugins: [
   231→        polar({
   232→            ...
   233→            use: [
   234→                checkout(...),
   235→                portal()
   236→            ],
   237→        })
   238→    ]
   239→});
   240→```
   241→
   242→The portal-plugin gives the BetterAuth Client a set of customer management methods, scoped under `authClient.customer`.
   243→
   244→### Customer Portal Management
   245→
   246→The following method will redirect the user to the Polar Customer Portal, where they can see orders, purchases, subscriptions, benefits, etc.
   247→
   248→```typescript
   249→await authClient.customer.portal();
   250→```
   251→
   252→### Customer State
   253→
   254→The portal plugin also adds a convenient state-method for retrieving the general Customer State.
   255→
   256→```typescript
   257→const { data: customerState } = await authClient.customer.state();
   258→```
   259→
   260→The customer state object contains:
   261→
   262→- All the data about the customer.
   263→- The list of their active subscriptions
   264→  - Note: This does not include subscriptions done by a parent organization. See the subscription list-method below for more information.
   265→- The list of their granted benefits.
   266→- The list of their active meters, with their current balance.
   267→
   268→Thus, with that single object, you have all the required information to check if you should provision access to your service or not.
   269→
   270→[You can learn more about the Polar Customer State in the Polar Docs](https://docs.polar.sh/integrate/customer-state).
   271→
   272→### Benefits, Orders & Subscriptions
   273→
   274→The portal plugin adds 3 convenient methods for listing benefits, orders & subscriptions relevant to the authenticated user/customer.
   275→
   276→[All of these methods use the Polar CustomerPortal APIs](https://docs.polar.sh/api-reference/customer-portal)
   277→
   278→#### Benefits
   279→
   280→This method only lists granted benefits for the authenticated user/customer.
   281→
   282→```typescript
   283→const { data: benefits } = await authClient.customer.benefits.list({
   284→  query: {
   285→    page: 1,
   286→    limit: 10,
   287→  },
   288→});
   289→```
   290→
   291→#### Orders
   292→
   293→This method lists orders like purchases and subscription renewals for the authenticated user/customer.
   294→
   295→```typescript
   296→const { data: orders } = await authClient.customer.orders.list({
   297→  query: {
   298→    page: 1,
   299→    limit: 10,
   300→    productBillingType: "one_time", // or 'recurring'
   301→  },
   302→});
   303→```
   304→
   305→#### Subscriptions
   306→
   307→This method lists the subscriptions associated with authenticated user/customer.
   308→
   309→```typescript
   310→const { data: subscriptions } = await authClient.customer.subscriptions.list({
   311→  query: {
   312→    page: 1,
   313→    limit: 10,
   314→    active: true,
   315→  },
   316→});
   317→```
   318→
   319→**Important** - Organization Support
   320→
   321→This will **not** return subscriptions made by a parent organization to the authenticated user.
   322→
   323→However, you can pass a `referenceId` to this method. This will return all subscriptions associated with that referenceId instead of subscriptions associated with the user.
   324→
   325→So in order to figure out if a user should have access, pass the user's organization ID to see if there is an active subscription for that organization.
   326→
   327→```typescript
   328→const organizationId = (await authClient.organization.list())?.data?.[0]?.id,
   329→
   330→const { data: subscriptions } = await authClient.customer.orders.list({
   331→    query: {
   332→	    page: 1,
   333→		limit: 10,
   334→		active: true,
   335→        referenceId: organizationId
   336→    },
   337→});
   338→
   339→const userShouldHaveAccess = subscriptions.some(
   340→    sub => // Your logic to check subscription product or whatever.
   341→)
   342→```
   343→
   344→## Usage Plugin
   345→
   346→A simple plugin for Usage Based Billing.
   347→
   348→```typescript
   349→import { polar, checkout, portal, usage } from "@polar-sh/better-auth";
   350→
   351→const auth = betterAuth({
   352→    // ... Better Auth config
   353→    plugins: [
   354→        polar({
   355→            ...
   356→            use: [
   357→                checkout(...),
   358→                portal(),
   359→                usage()
   360→            ],
   361→        })
   362→    ]
   363→});
   364→```
   365→
   366→### Event Ingestion
   367→
   368→Polar's Usage Based Billing builds entirely on event ingestion. Ingest events from your application, create Meters to represent that usage, and add metered prices to Products to charge for it.
   369→
   370→[Learn more about Usage Based Billing in the Polar Docs.](https://docs.polar.sh/features/usage-based-billing/introduction)
   371→
   372→```typescript
   373→const { data: ingested } = await authClient.usage.ingest({
   374→  event: "file-uploads",
   375→  metadata: {
   376→    uploadedFiles: 12,
   377→  },
   378→});
   379→```
   380→
   381→The authenticated user is automatically associated with the ingested event.
   382→
   383→### Customer Meters
   384→
   385→A simple method for listing the authenticated user's Usage Meters, or as we call them, Customer Meters.
   386→
   387→Customer Meter's contains all information about their consumption on your defined meters.
   388→
   389→- Customer Information
   390→- Meter Information
   391→- Customer Meter Information
   392→  - Consumed Units
   393→  - Credited Units
   394→  - Balance
   395→
   396→```typescript
   397→const { data: customerMeters } = await authClient.usage.meters.list({
   398→  query: {
   399→    page: 1,
   400→    limit: 10,
   401→  },
   402→});
   403→```
   404→
   405→## Webhooks Plugin
   406→
   407→The Webhooks plugin can be used to capture incoming events from your Polar organization.
   408→
   409→```typescript
   410→import { polar, webhooks } from "@polar-sh/better-auth";
   411→
   412→const auth = betterAuth({
   413→    // ... Better Auth config
   414→    plugins: [
   415→        polar({
   416→            ...
   417→            use: [
   418→                webhooks({
   419→                    secret: process.env.POLAR_WEBHOOK_SECRET,
   420→                    onCustomerStateChanged: (payload) => // Triggered when anything regarding a customer changes
   421→                    onOrderPaid: (payload) => // Triggered when an order was paid (purchase, subscription renewal, etc.)
   422→                    ...  // Over 25 granular webhook handlers
   423→                    onPayload: (payload) => // Catch-all for all events
   424→                })
   425→            ],
   426→        })
   427→    ]
   428→});
   429→```
   430→
   431→Configure a Webhook endpoint in your Polar Organization Settings page. Webhook endpoint is configured at /polar/webhooks.
   432→
   433→Add the secret to your environment.
   434→
   435→```bash
   436→# .env
   437→POLAR_WEBHOOK_SECRET=...
   438→```
   439→
   440→The plugin supports handlers for all Polar webhook events:
   441→
   442→- `onPayload` - Catch-all handler for any incoming Webhook event
   443→- `onCheckoutCreated` - Triggered when a checkout is created
   444→- `onCheckoutUpdated` - Triggered when a checkout is updated
   445→- `onOrderCreated` - Triggered when an order is created
   446→- `onOrderPaid` - Triggered when an order is paid
   447→- `onOrderRefunded` - Triggered when an order is refunded
   448→- `onRefundCreated` - Triggered when a refund is created
   449→- `onRefundUpdated` - Triggered when a refund is updated
   450→- `onSubscriptionCreated` - Triggered when a subscription is created
   451→- `onSubscriptionUpdated` - Triggered when a subscription is updated
   452→- `onSubscriptionActive` - Triggered when a subscription becomes active
   453→- `onSubscriptionCanceled` - Triggered when a subscription is canceled
   454→- `onSubscriptionRevoked` - Triggered when a subscription is revoked
   455→- `onSubscriptionUncanceled` - Triggered when a subscription cancellation is reversed
   456→- `onProductCreated` - Triggered when a product is created
   457→- `onProductUpdated` - Triggered when a product is updated
   458→- `onOrganizationUpdated` - Triggered when an organization is updated
   459→- `onBenefitCreated` - Triggered when a benefit is created
   460→- `onBenefitUpdated` - Triggered when a benefit is updated
   461→- `onBenefitGrantCreated` - Triggered when a benefit grant is created
   462→- `onBenefitGrantUpdated` - Triggered when a benefit grant is updated
   463→- `onBenefitGrantRevoked` - Triggered when a benefit grant is revoked
   464→- `onCustomerCreated` - Triggered when a customer is created
   465→- `onCustomerUpdated` - Triggered when a customer is updated
   466→- `onCustomerDeleted` - Triggered when a customer is deleted

1→---
     2→title: Two-Factor Authentication (2FA)
     3→description: Enhance your app's security with two-factor authentication.
     4→---
     5→
     6→`OTP` `TOTP` `Backup Codes` `Trusted Devices`
     7→
     8→Two-Factor Authentication (2FA) adds an extra security step when users log in. Instead of just using a password, they'll need to provide a second form of verification. This makes it much harder for unauthorized people to access accounts, even if they've somehow gotten the password.
     9→
    10→This plugin offers two main methods to do a second factor verification:
    11→
    12→1. **OTP (One-Time Password)**: A temporary code sent to the user's email or phone.
    13→2. **TOTP (Time-based One-Time Password)**: A code generated by an app on the user's device.
    14→
    15→**Additional features include:**
    16→- Generating backup codes for account recovery
    17→- Enabling/disabling 2FA
    18→- Managing trusted devices
    19→
    20→## Installation
    21→
    22→<Steps>
    23→    <Step>
    24→        ### Add the plugin to your auth config
    25→
    26→        Add the two-factor plugin to your auth configuration and specify your app name as the issuer.
    27→
    28→        ```ts title="auth.ts"
    29→        import { betterAuth } from "better-auth"
    30→        import { twoFactor } from "better-auth/plugins" // [!code highlight]
    31→
    32→        export const auth = betterAuth({
    33→            // ... other config options
    34→            appName: "My App", // provide your app name. It'll be used as an issuer. // [!code highlight]
    35→            plugins: [
    36→                twoFactor() // [!code highlight]
    37→            ]
    38→        })
    39→        ```
    40→    </Step>
    41→    <Step>
    42→        ### Migrate the database
    43→
    44→        Run the migration or generate the schema to add the necessary fields and tables to the database.
    45→
    46→        <Tabs items={["migrate", "generate"]}>
    47→            <Tab value="migrate">
    48→            ```package-install
    49→            npx auth migrate
    50→            ```
    51→            </Tab>
    52→            <Tab value="generate">
    53→            ```package-install
    54→            npx auth generate
    55→            ```
    56→            </Tab>
    57→        </Tabs>
    58→        See the [Schema](#schema) section to add the fields manually.
    59→    </Step>
    60→
    61→        <Step>
    62→        ### Add the client plugin
    63→
    64→        Add the client plugin and Specify where the user should be redirected if they need to verify 2nd factor
    65→
    66→        ```ts title="auth-client.ts"
    67→        import { createAuthClient } from "better-auth/client"
    68→        import { twoFactorClient } from "better-auth/client/plugins" // [!code highlight]
    69→
    70→        export const authClient = createAuthClient({
    71→            plugins: [
    72→                twoFactorClient() // [!code highlight]
    73→            ]
    74→        })
    75→        ```
    76→        </Step>
    77→</Steps>
    78→
    79→## Usage
    80→
    81→### Enabling 2FA
    82→
    83→To enable two-factor authentication, call `twoFactor.enable` with the user's password and issuer (optional):
    84→
    85→<APIMethod
    86→  path="/two-factor/enable"
    87→  method="POST"
    88→  requireSession
    89→>
    90→```ts
    91→type enableTwoFactor = {
    92→    /**
    93→     * The user's password
    94→     */
    95→    password: string = "secure-password"
    96→    /**
    97→     * An optional custom issuer for the TOTP URI. Defaults to app-name defined in your auth config.
    98→     */
    99→    issuer?: string = "my-app-name"
   100→}
   101→```
   102→</APIMethod>
   103→
   104→When 2FA is enabled:
   105→- An encrypted `secret` and `backupCodes` are generated.
   106→- `enable` returns `totpURI` and `backupCodes`.
   107→
   108→Note: `twoFactorEnabled` won’t be set to `true` until the user verifies their TOTP code. Learn more about verifying TOTP [here](#totp). You can skip verification by setting `skipVerificationOnEnable` to true in your plugin config.
   109→
   110→<Callout type="warn">
   111→Two Factor can only be enabled for credential accounts at the moment. For social accounts, it's assumed the provider already handles 2FA.
   112→</Callout>
   113→
   114→### Sign In with 2FA
   115→
   116→When a user with 2FA enabled tries to sign in via email, the response object will contain `twoFactorRedirect` set to `true`. This indicates that the user needs to verify their 2FA code.
   117→
   118→You can handle this in the `onSuccess` callback or by providing a `onTwoFactorRedirect` callback in the plugin config.
   119→
   120→```tsx
   121→import { authClient } from "@/lib/auth-client"
   122→
   123→await authClient.signIn.email({
   124→        email: "user@example.com",
   125→        password: "password123",
   126→    },
   127→    {
   128→        async onSuccess(context) {
   129→            if (context.data.twoFactorRedirect) {
   130→                // Handle the 2FA verification in place
   131→            }
   132→        },
   133→    }
   134→)
   135→```
   136→
   137→Using the `onTwoFactorRedirect` config:
   138→
   139→```ts title="auth-client.ts"
   140→import { createAuthClient } from "better-auth/client";
   141→import { twoFactorClient } from "better-auth/client/plugins";
   142→
   143→const authClient = createAuthClient({
   144→    plugins: [
   145→        twoFactorClient({
   146→            onTwoFactorRedirect(){
   147→                // Handle the 2FA verification globally
   148→            },
   149→        }),
   150→    ],
   151→});
   152→```
   153→
   154→
   155→
   156→
   157→<Callout type="warn">
   158→**With `auth.api`**
   159→
   160→When you call `auth.api.signInEmail` on the server, and the user has 2FA enabled, it will return an object where `twoFactorRedirect` is set to `true`. This behavior isn’t inferred in TypeScript, which can be misleading. You can check using `in` instead to check if `twoFactorRedirect` is set to `true`.
   161→
   162→```ts title="sign-in.ts"
   163→import { auth } from "@/lib/auth"
   164→
   165→const response = await auth.api.signInEmail({
   166→	body: {
   167→		email: "test@test.com",
   168→		password: "test",
   169→	},
   170→});
   171→
   172→if ("twoFactorRedirect" in response) {
   173→	// Handle the 2FA verification in place
   174→}
   175→```
   176→</Callout>
   177→
   178→### Disabling 2FA
   179→
   180→To disable two-factor authentication, call `twoFactor.disable` with the user's password:
   181→
   182→<APIMethod
   183→  path="/two-factor/disable"
   184→  method="POST"
   185→  requireSession
   186→>
   187→```ts
   188→type disableTwoFactor = {
   189→    /**
   190→     * The user's password
   191→     */
   192→    password: string
   193→}
   194→```
   195→</APIMethod>
   196→
   197→### TOTP
   198→
   199→TOTP (Time-Based One-Time Password) is an algorithm that generates a unique password for each login attempt using time as a counter. Every fixed interval (Better Auth defaults to 30 seconds), a new password is generated. This addresses several issues with traditional passwords: they can be forgotten, stolen, or guessed. OTPs solve some of these problems, but their delivery via SMS or email can be unreliable (or even risky, considering it opens new attack vectors).
   200→
   201→TOTP, however, generates codes offline, making it both secure and convenient. You just need an authenticator app on your phone.
   202→
   203→#### Getting TOTP URI
   204→
   205→After enabling 2FA, you can get the TOTP URI to display to the user. This URI is generated by the server using the `secret` and `issuer` and can be used to generate a QR code for the user to scan with their authenticator app.
   206→
   207→<APIMethod
   208→  path="/two-factor/get-totp-uri"
   209→  method="POST"
   210→  requireSession
   211→>
   212→```ts
   213→type getTOTPURI = {
   214→    /**
   215→     * The user's password
   216→     */
   217→    password: string
   218→}
   219→```
   220→</APIMethod>
   221→
   222→
   223→**Example: Using React**
   224→
   225→Once you have the TOTP URI, you can use it to generate a QR code for the user to scan with their authenticator app.
   226→
   227→```tsx
   228→import { authClient } from "@/lib/auth-client"
   229→import QRCode from "react-qr-code";
   230→
   231→export default function UserCard({ password }: { password: string }){
   232→    const { data: session } = authClient.useSession();
   233→	const { data: qr } = useQuery({
   234→		queryKey: ["two-factor-qr"],
   235→		queryFn: async () => {
   236→			const res = await authClient.twoFactor.getTotpUri({ password });
   237→			return res.data;
   238→		},
   239→		enabled: !!session?.user.twoFactorEnabled,
   240→	});
   241→    return (
   242→        <QRCode value={qr?.totpURI || ""} />
   243→   )
   244→}
   245→```
   246→
   247→<Callout>
   248→By default the issuer for TOTP is set to the app name provided in the auth config or if not provided it will be set to `Better Auth`. You can override this by passing `issuer` to the plugin config.
   249→</Callout>
   250→
   251→#### Verifying TOTP
   252→
   253→After the user has entered their 2FA code, you can verify it using `twoFactor.verifyTotp` method. `Better Auth` follows standard practice by accepting TOTP codes from one period before and one after the current code, ensuring users can authenticate even with minor time delays on their end.
   254→
   255→<APIMethod path="/two-factor/verify-totp" method="POST">
   256→```ts
   257→type verifyTOTP = {
   258→    /**
   259→     * The otp code to verify. 
   260→     */
   261→    code: string = "012345"
   262→    /**
   263→     * If true, the device will be trusted for 30 days. It'll be refreshed on every sign in request within this time. 
   264→     */
   265→    trustDevice?: boolean = true
   266→}
   267→```
   268→</APIMethod>
   269→
   270→### OTP
   271→
   272→OTP (One-Time Password) is similar to TOTP but a random code is generated and sent to the user's email or phone.
   273→
   274→Before using OTP to verify the second factor, you need to configure `sendOTP` in your Better Auth instance. This function is responsible for sending the OTP to the user's email, phone, or any other method supported by your application.
   275→
   276→```ts title="auth.ts"
   277→import { betterAuth } from "better-auth"
   278→import { twoFactor } from "better-auth/plugins"
   279→
   280→export const auth = betterAuth({
   281→    plugins: [
   282→        twoFactor({
   283→          	otpOptions: {
   284→				async sendOTP({ user, otp }, ctx) {
   285→                    // send otp to user
   286→				},
   287→			},
   288→        })
   289→    ]
   290→})
   291→```
   292→
   293→#### Sending OTP
   294→
   295→Sending an OTP is done by calling the `twoFactor.sendOtp` function. This function will trigger your sendOTP implementation that you provided in the Better Auth configuration.
   296→
   297→<APIMethod path="/two-factor/send-otp" method="POST">
   298→```ts
   299→type send2FaOTP = {
   300→    /**
   301→     * If true, the device will be trusted for 30 days. It'll be refreshed on every sign in request within this time. 
   302→     */
   303→    trustDevice?: boolean = true
   304→}
   305→
   306→if (data) {
   307→    // redirect or show the user to enter the code
   308→}
   309→```
   310→</APIMethod>
   311→
   312→#### Verifying OTP
   313→
   314→After the user has entered their OTP code, you can verify it
   315→
   316→<APIMethod path="/two-factor/verify-otp" method="POST">
   317→```ts
   318→type verifyOTP = {
   319→    /**
   320→     * The otp code to verify. 
   321→     */
   322→    code: string = "012345"
   323→    /**
   324→     * If true, the device will be trusted for 30 days. It'll be refreshed on every sign in request within this time. 
   325→     */
   326→    trustDevice?: boolean = true
   327→}
   328→```
   329→</APIMethod>
   330→
   331→### Backup Codes
   332→
   333→Backup codes are generated and stored in the database. This can be used to recover access to the account if the user loses access to their phone or email.
   334→
   335→#### Generating Backup Codes
   336→Generate backup codes for account recovery:
   337→
   338→<APIMethod
   339→  path="/two-factor/generate-backup-codes"
   340→  method="POST"
   341→  requireSession
   342→>
   343→```ts
   344→type generateBackupCodes = {
   345→    /**
   346→     * The users password. 
   347→     */
   348→    password: string
   349→}
   350→
   351→if (data) {
   352→    // Show the backup codes to the user
   353→}
   354→```
   355→</APIMethod>
   356→
   357→
   358→<Callout type="warn">
   359→When you generate backup codes, the old backup codes will be deleted and new ones will be generated.
   360→</Callout>
   361→
   362→#### Using Backup Codes
   363→
   364→You can now allow users to provide a backup code as an account recovery method.
   365→
   366→
   367→<APIMethod path="/two-factor/verify-backup-code" method="POST">
   368→```ts
   369→type verifyBackupCode = {
   370→    /**
   371→     * A backup code to verify. 
   372→     */
   373→    code: string = "123456"
   374→    /**
   375→     * If true, the session cookie will not be set. 
   376→     */
   377→    disableSession?: boolean = false
   378→    /**
   379→     * If true, the device will be trusted for 30 days. It'll be refreshed on every sign in request within this time. 
   380→     */
   381→    trustDevice?: boolean = true
   382→}
   383→```
   384→</APIMethod>
   385→
   386→<Callout>
   387→Once a backup code is used, it will be removed from the database and can't be used again.
   388→</Callout>
   389→
   390→#### Viewing Backup Codes
   391→
   392→To display the backup codes to the user, you can call `viewBackupCodes` on the server. This will return the backup codes in the response. You should only do this if the user has a fresh session - a session that was just created.
   393→
   394→<APIMethod
   395→  path="/two-factor/view-backup-codes"
   396→  method="POST"
   397→  isServerOnly
   398→  forceAsBody
   399→>
   400→```ts
   401→type viewBackupCodes = {
   402→    /**
   403→     * The user ID to view all backup codes. 
   404→     */
   405→    userId?: string | null = "user-id"
   406→}
   407→```
   408→</APIMethod>
   409→
   410→### Trusted Devices
   411→
   412→You can mark a device as trusted by passing `trustDevice` to `verifyTotp` or `verifyOtp`.
   413→
   414→```ts
   415→const verify2FA = async (code: string) => {
   416→    const { data, error } = await authClient.twoFactor.verifyTotp({
   417→        code,
   418→        trustDevice: true, // Mark this device as trusted // [!code highlight]
   419→    })
   420→    if (data) {
   421→        // 2FA verified and device trusted
   422→    }
   423→}
   424→```
   425→
   426→When `trustDevice` is set to `true`, the current device will be remembered for 30 days. During this period, the user won't be prompted for 2FA on subsequent sign-ins from this device. The trust period is refreshed each time the user signs in successfully.
   427→
   428→### Issuer
   429→
   430→By adding an `issuer` you can set your application name for the 2fa application.
   431→
   432→For example, if your user uses Google Auth, the default appName will show up as `Better Auth`. However, by using the following code, it will show up as `my-app-name`.
   433→
   434→```ts
   435→twoFactor({
   436→    issuer: "my-app-name" // [!code highlight]
   437→})
   438→```
   439→---
   440→
   441→## Schema
   442→
   443→The plugin requires 1 additional field in the `user` table and 1 additional table to store the two factor authentication data.
   444→
   445→Table: `user`
   446→
   447→<DatabaseTable
   448→    fields={[
   449→        { name: "twoFactorEnabled", type: "boolean", description: "Whether two factor authentication is enabled for the user.", isOptional: true },
   450→    ]}
   451→/>
   452→
   453→Table: `twoFactor`
   454→
   455→<DatabaseTable
   456→    fields={[
   457→        { name: "id", type: "string", description: "The ID of the two factor authentication.", isPrimaryKey: true },
   458→        { name: "userId", type: "string", description: "The ID of the user", isForeignKey: true },
   459→        { name: "secret", type: "string", description: "The secret used to generate the TOTP code.", isOptional: true },
   460→        { name: "backupCodes", type: "string", description: "The backup codes used to recover access to the account if the user loses access to their phone or email.", isOptional: true },
   461→    ]}
   462→/>
   463→
   464→## Options
   465→
   466→### Server
   467→
   468→**twoFactorTable**: The name of the table that stores the two factor authentication data. Default: `twoFactor`.
   469→
   470→**skipVerificationOnEnable**: Skip the verification process before enabling two factor for a user.
   471→
   472→**Issuer**: The issuer is the name of your application. It's used to generate TOTP codes. It'll be displayed in the authenticator apps.
   473→
   474→**TOTP options**
   475→
   476→these are options for TOTP.
   477→
   478→<TypeTable
   479→  type={{
   480→    digits:{
   481→        description: "The number of digits the otp to be",
   482→        type: "number",
   483→        default: 6,
   484→    },
   485→    period: {
   486→        description: "The period for totp in seconds.",
   487→        type: "number",
   488→        default: 30,
   489→    },
   490→  }}
   491→/>
   492→
   493→**OTP options**
   494→
   495→these are options for OTP.
   496→
   497→<TypeTable
   498→  type={{
   499→    sendOTP: {
   500→        description: "a function that sends the otp to the user's email or phone number. It takes two parameters: user and otp",
   501→        type: "function",
   502→    },
   503→    period: {
   504→        description: "The period for otp in minutes.", 
   505→        type: "number",
   506→        default: 3,
   507→    },
   508→    storeOTP: {
   509→        description: "How to store the otp in the database. Whether to store it as plain text, encrypted or hashed. You can also provide a custom encryptor or hasher.",
   510→        type: "string",
   511→        default: "plain",
   512→    },
   513→  }}
   514→  />
   515→
   516→**Backup Code Options**
   517→
   518→backup codes are generated and stored in the database when the user enabled two factor authentication. This can be used to recover access to the account if the user loses access to their phone or email.
   519→
   520→<TypeTable
   521→    type={{
   522→        amount: {
   523→            description: "The amount of backup codes to generate",
   524→            type: "number",
   525→            default: 10,
   526→        },
   527→        length: {
   528→            description: "The length of the backup codes",
   529→            type: "number",
   530→            default: 10,
   531→        },
   532→        customBackupCodesGenerate: {
   533→            description: "A function that generates custom backup codes. It takes no parameters and returns an array of strings.",
   534→            type: "function",
   535→        },
   536→        storeBackupCodes: {
   537→            description: "How to store the backup codes in the database. Whether to store it as plain text or encrypted. You can also provide a custom encryptor.",
   538→            type: "string",
   539→            default: "plain",
   540→        },
   541→    }}
   542→/>
   543→
   544→### Client
   545→
   546→To use the two factor plugin in the client, you need to add it on your plugins list.
   547→
   548→```ts title="auth-client.ts"
   549→import { createAuthClient } from "better-auth/client"
   550→import { twoFactorClient } from "better-auth/client/plugins"
   551→
   552→const authClient =  createAuthClient({
   553→    plugins: [
   554→        twoFactorClient({ // [!code highlight]
   555→            onTwoFactorRedirect(){ // [!code highlight]
   556→                window.location.href = "/2fa" // Handle the 2FA verification redirect // [!code highlight]
   557→            } // [!code highlight]
   558→        }) // [!code highlight]
   559→    ]
   560→})
   561→```
   562→
   563→
   564→**Options**
   565→
   566→`onTwoFactorRedirect`: A callback that will be called when the user needs to verify their 2FA code. This can be used to redirect the user to the 2FA page.
